elements.element: Vendor duty to defend (not merely indemnify) Customer
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client"

elements.element: Indemnified parties include Customer and its affiliates
elements.evidence: "Client and its affiliates, directors, officers, employees and agents"

elements.element: Covers third-party claims alleging services or deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any deliverable furnished by TrueLink infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of law
elements.evidence: "(ii) TrueLink's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation"

elements.element: Covers data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "(iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Client Confidential Information caused by TrueLink"

elements.element: Covers Vendor gross negligence / wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "(iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct"
"shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim"
"allow the indemnifying party to control the defense"
"provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense"

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: Clause 12.a remains open-ended: "Client shall indemnify and hold TrueLink ... harmless from and against all claims ... arising from or relating to the following:" — untouched by the redline

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: No amendment to 12.a; the inserted paragraph c only addresses TrueLink's obligations ("Without limiting the foregoing, TrueLink shall defend...")
"(i) an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services ... infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Exclusion for Customer modifications and combinations
elements.evidence: "to the extent the claim arises from Client Content or from Client's unauthorized modification or combination of the Interface"
Exclusions listed are only "Client Content or from Client's unauthorized modification or combination"; no specifications carve-out

elements.element: IP remedies: procure, modify, replace, refund
elements.evidence: No remedy mechanic appears anywhere in the inserted text

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: Insertion contains no cap; comment only says "we can discuss a super-cap on this indemnity if helpful" (non-operative)

offending_extra_words: (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or admission on the indemnified party shall be made without its prior written consent)
reasons: Preferred level incomplete: the existing Customer indemnity at 12.a is left uncapped in scope, whereas the preferred position requires Customer's indemnity to be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. The condition is present (a Customer indemnity exists), so this element cannot be treated as absent.
Fallback level is also incomplete (no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no specifications exclusion, no 3× annual fees super-cap), so the redline does not land on either complete bargain.

Minimality fails: the insertion adds hold-harmless language, indemnitees beyond Customer and affiliates (directors, officers, employees, agents), and settlement-consent mechanics beyond the preferred notice/control/cooperation procedure.

Intent is preserved: the untouched paragraphs a and b remain effective and the insertion introduces no contradiction, though it relies on 'Client Content' and 'Support Services' being defined elsewhere in the agreement.
